entries.title: RULES.md is the sole rulebook; read README.md then RULES.md before any work
entries.text: Read root README.md and RULES.md completely at session start and after compaction. RULES.md is the only authority for safety, production-data compatibility (rule 11: expand-first migrations, no destructive changes without a separate maintainer decision), no new source comments (rule 9), critical-only tests (rule 10), Git identity and authorization (rule 14), and verification. Never deploy, touch the VPS, move real money, or send real customer mail. This tally entry points there and does not restate or override it.

entries.title: Maintainer decision 2026-11-13: AutoPay and normal online payments stay disabled until the maintainer enables them
entries.text: Decision (maintainer, 2026-11-13, in chat): AutoPay and normal (one-time gateway checkout) payments are turned off for the time being and remain disabled unless the maintainer decides to activate them. Agents never enable them, never change payment env keys, and never treat a fix as permission to re-enable. Implications for planning: admin offline recording (recordContribution, incl. the new monthly-investment category) is the primary way investments enter the ledger; the AutoPay next_due_date bug (finding-6) becomes a must-fix-before-re-enable item rather than urgent; DD point 6 SIP months-paid must count offline-recorded monthly investments to be meaningful; question row 7 (AutoPay on web) is deferred. Known switches (STATIC): AutoPay via PHONEPE_AUTOPAY_ENABLED / PHONEPE_AUTOPAY_COLLECTION_ENABLED (default false, environment.ts:101-102); one-time checkout has no dedicated flag, only removing the relay (PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL/SECRET) which makes POST pay return a generic DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE (clientOrderRoutes.ts:154-156). To be recorded in the next plan's decision record.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13 (Q1): keep client and investment records on dev and prod; prod data reform via tested one-time step
entries.text: Maintainer answer to question row 1. Dev server may be cleaned, but on BOTH dev and production client records and investment records stay intact. Production manages real clients. Approach: save a copy of the required information from the production database, then in the next deployed update run a one-time migration/copy step that reforms the database with proper client data without losing any of it; rehearse that step on the dev server first. Constraints from RULES: the maintainer performs every production export and deploy (rule 2/3); a reform that rewrites, backfills or removes rows is a destructive change under rule 11 needing the recorded pre-flight check, refusal-on-loss, populated-upgrade test and rollback-boundary registration; ledger/order/payment/audit/consent/application/delivery rows are never deleted or rewritten, corrections are new rows. Open: what exactly is wrong in the current data (follow-up question), and how production PII copied to dev is protected.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13 (Q2): clients see each admin recording as a receipt labelled by its category
entries.text: Maintainer answer to question row 2. When the admin records an investment (earlier investment, correction, monthly investment, and further categories), the client sees it like a receipt, labelled with the category the admin chose. Implementation must stay additive so released APKs keep working (RULES rule 11): prefer a new client endpoint/screen and category-aware notification over changing existing response shapes or enums, unless the design check shows the change is tolerated. The notification text must follow the category instead of the fixed 'before you joined the app' copy.
entries.retiredWhy: Question answers are decisions, not rules (maintainer 2026-11-14). Recorded as decision DEC-2, group admin-improvements.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13 (Q3): no automatic maturity; admin maturity dates, dashboard, prompt on every admin open
entries.text: Maintainer answer to question row 3. No automatic maturity. Admin enters a maturity date. A specialised maturity management dashboard lists them. When a maturity date nears, the admin is notified every time the admin app is opened and asked to resolve it with one of: (1) return all the money to the client; (2) record it as a one-time investment that starts from the maturity date and from then start a new SIP; (3) reinvest the money as a SIP. Every recording counts; the admin manages and updates them. No payout or ledger change ever happens without the admin's explicit resolution. Real bank transfer stays outside the app (existing withdrawal payout flow).

entries.title: Decisions 2026-11-13 (Q4-Q8): nominee+relation, onboarding only, reviews, AutoPay off, growth records notify clients
entries.text: Maintainer answers. Q4: nominee name with relation to the account holder. Q5: public signups are not in use; only admin onboarding of clients is used, so DD point 3 (signup redirect) is not pursued; audit the onboarding process for bugs. Q6: signup application reviews stay as they are; admin onboarding works well today and does not go through review (answer did not address DD point 1 client app reviews/comments; follow-up question). Q7: AutoPay stays off until the maintainer says so (see rule-2); AutoPay-on-web not pursued. Q8: value updates are entered monthly as the amount increased since investment; keep EACH update as a record and notify the client every time their investment is updated. ROI form (simple vs annualised) not answered; default simple return %.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13: plans/admin-improvements.md approved; Phase A starts on parallel tracks
entries.text: Maintainer replied 'Yes I do' to: approve the plan, commit it, and start Phase A on tally tracks with their own worktrees. Covers opening tracks/worktrees, npm ci of locked dependencies inside them for one-shot checks, committing on track branches and landing through the tally queue onto local main (not pushing). Not covered: container runtime for the testcontainers integration suite (gate G2), deploys, APK exports, real customer mail, enabling payments, Phase D destructive step, identity rule changes pending Q-017/Q-024/Q-025. Lane rules: adminQueries.ts must not grow (move touched hooks into feature query modules); admin-money.ts untouched in Phase A; new contract files per lane in Phase B; migrations 061/062/063 reserved for C1/C2/C3.

entries.title: Decisions 2026-11-13 (second round): containers, SIP, maturity, identity, data reform, reviews, ROI
entries.text: Maintainer answers via in-chat questions, 2026-11-13. G2: container runtime allowed for the testcontainers integration suite (throwaway PostgreSQL, cleaned up). Q-021: admin-tracked SIP schedule (monthly amount, fund, start month, months; monthly recordings linked to a month; client sees N of M paid; no collection); maturity date per client fund holding. Q-024: BOTH an audited admin contact-correction action for clients who have not set a password (old links retired, new invite to corrected address) AND closed accounts releasing their email/phone. Q-017: admin invite (set) links valid 24 hours; email codes and reset links stay 10 minutes. Q-025: setting the password through the invite link marks that email verified. Q-019: reform fixes duplicates and fills missing new details (categories, maturity dates, SIP schedules, nominees); dev copy has names/emails/phones masked. Duplicates: duplicate investments get reversal entries keeping both rows; duplicate client accounts are closed and merged into the real one only after the maintainer confirms each pair. Q-020: client reviews wanted, admins only, with client profile; nothing public. Q-022: dashboards show simple return % as main figure plus annualised (XIRR) secondary. Q-023: app-update mail keeps going to all active clients.

entries.title: Decisions 2026-11-13 (revised): invites, verification, reform scope, bank-transfer investing, reviews later
entries.text: Supersedes rule-8 where they differ. In force: containers allowed for the integration suite; admin-tracked SIP schedule (amount, fund, start month, months; monthly recordings linked; client sees N of M paid; no collection); maturity date per client fund holding; admin contact correction before password set + closed accounts release email/phone (history kept); dashboards show simple % plus XIRR; app-update mail to all. REVISED: Q-017 invite links stay short (10 min); instead the admin must be able to regenerate a new invite link easily, incl. after expiry or cancellation. Q-025 setting a password does NOT verify the email; the email code step stays. Q-019 no standalone cleanup project: reform/clean the DB only when something requires it, client data only, no data lost, rehearsed on dev with masked copy. Clients pay SIPs and investments directly to the company bank account; the admin records them and clients must see invested amounts reflected seamlessly in their dashboard whether the gateway is on or off. Q-020 reviews wanted but deferred; fix bugs first. Maintainer delegates: work out what else such apps need and simplify complex flows so client and admin have a seamless experience.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13 (G12): expire stale pending online payments whose pay-by time has passed
entries.text: Maintainer chose: mark old pending online payments/orders created before payments were turned off as expired. Scope: only attempts/payments whose checkout expiry (plus the configured grace) has passed; one-time or reconciliation-pass step that uses the existing expiry path (paymentsRepository markPaymentExpired and the canonical outcome flow), audited, idempotent, never deletes or rewrites rows, never moves money, and never touches a payment the provider might still settle once payments return (if the gateway is later configured, normal reconciliation applies). Clients stop seeing 'awaiting payment'. This retires in-flight state deliberately under RULES rule 11 with the impact stated: those clients would have to start a new payment once payments return. Needs an integration test proving only expired-by-time rows change.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13: no bank details or payment instructions; monthly investments notify 'Investment added'
entries.text:
Maintainer, in chat during Phase B: "I wouldn't be adding/recording any bank details or payment methods included, only a category that adding monthly investments which for the clients will be receiving notifications as investment added." Effects:
- G11 no longer includes a How-to-invest FAQ. The maintainer's only remaining G11 step is publishing featureFlags.onlinePayments=false after B8 lands.
- B8 drops the How-to-invest card and any copy telling clients how or where to pay. Pay/invest buttons are still hidden when the flag is false, with at most one neutral line ("recorded by the BeOnEdge team").
- B1: monthly investment (and earlier investment) recordings notify the client with the title "Investment added". Correction keeps neutral wording.
- Agents never put bank details or payment methods in code, copy, FAQ seeds or emails.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13: recorded investments also email the client the amount with 'check your app'
entries.text:
Maintainer, in chat: "Also an email notification of the amount recorded for that client notifying about the investment added to their app, and to check their app." Effects:
- When the admin records a monthly or earlier investment, the client gets an email titled "Investment added", in addition to the in-app notification. It gives the amount (from paise), fund and date, asks them to open the app, and includes the CLIENT_WEB_APP_URL line when configured.
- Corrections send no email.
- Delivery: one email per recording, queued in the recording transaction, idempotent on replay. Amount and names go in the sealed payload. A per-template send guard cancels after reversal, closure or tombstone, bound to the email revision at queue time.
- Needs migration 062, which only widens the email_deliveries.template_check list. AdminEmailTemplateKey is a request filter, so the delivery response stays z.string() and released admin APKs are safe.
- Built by lane b-receipts. No bank details or payment instructions (rule-11).

entries.title: Decisions 2026-11-14: payments halted, no reference number, recordings confirmed, maturity choices for client
entries.text:
Maintainer, in chat, answering question rows 16-18:
- Payments: "i don't want to add or change anything about it, only asked you to fix some bugs and disable it." AutoPay and everything payment-gateway related is halted until the maintainer says to resume. E2 stays as built and dormant; no further payment work. Row 17 (missed AutoPay months) is answered by this: no change.
- Row 16: no reference number (UTR or any other) on admin recordings. Task E4-bank-reference is dropped.
- Recordings confirmed as built (B1/B2/B5): the Record action on the admin user page offers a Monthly investment category; every recording is kept with its date as a ledger/log the admin keeps, reflected in the client's app. Gap: the admin ledger tab shows the effective date only, not when the row was recorded.
- Row 18 maturity: options are (1) withdraw the invested amount with returns; (2) reinvest the previous amount as a one-time investment, then start recording the next SIP; (3) increase the SIP's time period (replaces "reinvest as a new SIP"). Options never pop up for the client by themselves. The admin is notified first (30-day launch prompt, confirmed), then either resolves directly after talking to the client, or sends the options to that client, who gets an email and an in-app notification and can choose in the app. Both client and admin can decide.

entries.title: Never enable payments or AutoPay; no payment or gateway work until the maintainer resumes it
entries.text: Never enable AutoPay or online payments, never change payment configuration or payment env keys, and do no payment, AutoPay or gateway work until the maintainer says to resume it. A fix is never permission to re-enable. Admin recording is how investments enter the ledger. Source: decisions DEC-22 and DEC-14 (group admin-improvements).

entries.title: No bank details, payment methods, payment instructions or reference numbers anywhere
entries.text: Never put bank details, payment methods or payment instructions in code, copy, FAQ seeds or emails, and never add a reference number (UTR or other) to investments the admin records. Source: decisions DEC-25 and DEC-13 (group admin-improvements).
